summary: Construct the mixed-characteristic classical GL_n correspondence by independent nearby-cycle character identities, prove the supercuspidal bijection and pair-factor compatibility, and then reconstruct full Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne parameters through the existing segment classification. Distinguish the essentially square-integrable Jacquet–Langlands bijection, the additive Langlands–Jacquet quotient, and the inner-form parameter from standard data. Import raw compact-unitary geometry before local comparison, and place cyclic base change and twisted character theory upstream of every consumer.

nodes.title: The classical normalization dictionary
nodes.statement: Fix F/Q_p finite, residue cardinality q, a uniformizer ϖ, geometric Φ in W_F, and ω(w)=q^{deg(w)}, with arithmetic degree +1 and deg(Φ)=−1. Use Art_geo:F×→W_F^ab sending ϖ to Φ; it equals arithmetic reciprocity composed with inversion on the abelianization. Fix the positive complex square root of q, and put σ(π)=rec_un(π)⊗ω^{(1−n)/2}. Normalized parabolic induction uses δ_P^{1/2}. For a WD object D=(V,r,N), L(s,D)=det(1−q^{−s}r(Φ)|(ker N)^I)^{−1}; ε(s,D,ψ) is the imported Deligne local constant with its monodromy determinant, with ψ-self-dual additive Haar measure. All analytic and Galois ε-functions use the same AL.1 Tate s-variable, not an unspecified scalar normalization.
hypotheses: n≥1; complex coefficients; nontrivial continuous additive ψ; multiplicative maximal compact volume 1.
proofSteps: Import the local Weil group and both reciprocity normalizations from current ClassFieldTheory, and the existing WD factor definitions from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations.
Compute the half-twist once: rec_un=σ⊗ω^{(n−1)/2}; compare every induction, dual and similitude factor with this equation.
At rank one identify Deligne’s constant with AL.1’s Tate epsilon, including the Haar measure and s-variable.
acceptance: For a rank-one χ, σ(χ)=χ∘Art_geo^{-1}; a uniformizer acts through χ(ϖ).

nodes.title: Strict O-module deformations with Drinfeld levels
nodes.statement: For r≥1 and β∈GL_n(O_r)diag(ϖ,1,…,1)GL_n(O_r), let H_β be the height-n, dimension-one strict ϖ-divisible O-module over κ_r with relative contravariant Dieudonné F=βσ. Instantiate its marked deformation ring R_β and Drinfeld level-m cover R_β,m: the n sections X_i of H[ϖ^m] satisfy the full relative Cartier-divisor identity ∑_{a∈(O/ϖ^m)^n}[∑a_iX_i]=[H[ϖ^m]]. Then R_β≃O_r[[T_1,…,T_{n−1}]] noncanonically; the finite level cover is regular and generically étale with GL_n(O/ϖ^m)-action. The formal level space may have several components. It has an equivariant finite-type algebraization along a finite special-fibre subscheme, as in Scholze Theorem 2.4.
hypotheses: The O-action on Lie H agrees with the structural O-action; κ_r has the specified κ-embedding; marked deformations preserve that strict action.
proofSteps: Apply the contravariant Dieudonné supplier with its requested strict relative O-linear extension. Relative F=βσ and the étale norm parameter F=β⁻¹σ₀ use different β conventions and opposite endomorphism algebras; both are contravariant.
Use the formal O-module deformation and Cartier-level representability supplier; connected–étale splitting reduces regularity and dimension to the connected case.
Use strict truncated-O-module algebraization, Artin approximation and normalization as in Theorem 2.4; request these exact deformation exports rather than duplicate their general owners.
acceptance: The relative deformation dimension is n−1; the GL_n(O/ϖ^m)-torsor assertion concerns the generic fibre.

nodes.title: The nearby-cycle test function
nodes.statement: Let τ∈Φ^r I_F with r≥1, h∈C_c^∞(GL_n(O),Q), and ℓ≠p. Form [RΨ_β]=∑_i(−1)^i lim_m H^0(R^iψ_{Spf R_β,m} Q̄_ℓ), with commuting W_{F_r} and compact-group actions. Set h∨(g)=h((g^{-1})^t) and φ_{τ,h}(β)=tr(τ×h∨|[RΨ_β]) on the preceding β-coset, zero elsewhere. Interpret the convolution trace at a finite level fixing h. Define f_{τ,h} as any cyclic-transfer representative with matching twisted orbital integrals, an element of the orbital-integral quotient rather than a distinguished test function.
hypotheses: Choose Q̄_ℓ≃C only after rationality; compact-group Haar volume is 1; τ has positive geometric Frobenius exponent.
proofSteps: Use the formal-to-adic nearby-cycle comparison and finite-level cohomology, then pass through level invariants.
Take alternating traces with the inverse-transpose h convention; transfer using the accepted cyclic fundamental-lemma/transfer node.
Independence of the transfer representative on representation traces uses the requested p-adic character and density theory.

nodes.statement: For every preceding τ,h, φ_{τ,h} is compactly supported, locally constant, Q-valued and independent of ℓ and the embedding Q̄_ℓ≃C. For a fixed normal level K under which h is biinvariant, its trace is the finite sum vol(K)∑_{g∈GL_n(O)/K}h(g)tr(τ×g∨|RΨ_β^K). Thus denominators are permitted for rational h and normalized convolution; integrality of a virtual Weil multiplicity is a separate result, not integrality of every rational-valued test function.

Apply the congruence-near-identity cohomology invariance theorem to prove local constancy in β.

Twist by the finite compact-group action and apply the ℓ-independent alternating trace theorem; the rational trace argument is Scholze Theorem 2.6. The controlled-cohomology variant gives the same mechanism in Deformations Propositions 3.15, 4.2–4.3.

nodes.title: Dieudonné norms in the étale and basic cases
nodes.statement: For a finite semisimple Q_p-algebra A with maximal order O_A, integral σ₀-conjugacy classes of β∈(O_A⊗Z_{p^r})× parametrize étale O_A^op-linear p-divisible groups H over F_{p^r} for which H[p] is free of rank one over O_A^op/p. The contravariant Dieudonné module is O_A⊗Z_{p^r}, with F=β⁻¹σ₀. The geometric descent operator γ=α∘Frob_H^{−r} determines an O_A×-conjugacy class Nβ. The characteristic polynomials of Nβ and ββ^{σ₀}⋯β^{σ₀^{r−1}} agree; this does not specify an element-valued norm in a noncommutative algebra. For the relative basic case let D/F have invariant 1/n, normalize v_D(ϖ)=n, and let B_r be the basic β in the deformation coset. Marking the unique geometric height-n formal O-module gives descent in D_{−r}; invert it to obtain the O_D×-conjugacy class Nβ in D_r={d:v_D(d)=r}.
hypotheses: r≥1; σ_0 is arithmetic Witt Frobenius; σ is relative arithmetic Frobenius in the O-module case.
proofSteps: Track contravariance, the opposite endomorphism algebra and the inverse β parameter when passing from relative F=βσ to the étale F=β⁻¹σ₀ description; no covariant Dieudonné functor is used.
Use integral Dieudonné classification for the étale case; conjugate marked lattices produce the same norm class.
In the basic case classify geometric formal modules, identify endomorphism height with v_D, and invert the negative-height descent operator.
acceptance: The arithmetic Witt Frobenius is distinct from the geometric Weil element in the trace.

nodes.statement: For h invariant under maximal-order units, φ_h(β)=h(Nβ) has matching twisted/ordinary orbital integrals in both the étale integral-algebra case and the basic B_r↔D_r case. Choose maximal compact volume 1 on the ambient groups and compact stabilizer volume 1 on each centralizer. Then ∫φ_h=∫h, with the integration domains respectively the unit groups or B_r,D_r. The basic identity is restricted to basic classes and the matched centralizer measures.

proofSteps: Write both orbital integrals as sums over marked integral Dieudonné lattices modulo the common quasi-isogeny group.
Use the fact that each lattice stabilizer is maximal compact to identify the same weighted sum.
Apply the requested untwisted and twisted Weyl integration formulas to obtain the integral equality.

nodes.title: Connected–étale descent of nearby cycles
nodes.statement: For H_β=H_β^0×H_β^et of connected height k, 1≤k≤n, level-m components are indexed by surjections v:(O/ϖ^m)^n→H_β^et[ϖ^m]. For a fixed rank-k kernel V, its stabilizer is P_V(O/ϖ^m). The corresponding formal pieces are power-series extensions by n−k variables of the connected height-k deformation space. Nearby cycles are canonically the connected nearby cycles tensored with the finite regular representation of GL_{n−k}(O/ϖ^m), inducing a virtual compact-group identity [RΨ_β]=Ind_{P_k(O)}^{GL_n(O)}([RΨ_{β^0}]⊗C_c^∞(GL_{n−k}(O))). In the final h-trace formula the étale norm acts by right multiplication by (Nβ^et)^{-1}; retain the transposed action on the undualized sheaf.
hypotheses: Use the contravariant β convention and inverse-transpose h; no k=0 formal dimension-one object occurs.
proofSteps: Separate connected and étale torsion and classify surjective level maps and their kernels.
Use formal smoothness of the connected-part projection and invariance of nearby cycles under a formal disc.
Induce over the compact group and dualize the compact action to obtain the specified right multiplication in the trace.
acceptance: k=n gives the original connected nearby cycles and a trivial étale factor; k=1<n retains the finite regular étale factor.

For π=i_P^{GL_n}(π_1⊠⋯⊠π_t), t≥2, with irreducible blocks of ranks n_i, the transferred test trace is tr(f_{τ,h}|π)=tr(τ|⊕_i rec_un(π_i)⊗ω^{(n−n_i)/2})tr(h|π). The trace on an induced finite-length representation is additive; the constituent-level conclusion uses the type-and-density reduction. In the unnormalized Jacquet-module calculation each connected height-k term carries the modulus factor q^{(n−k)r}, where q=|κ_F|.
hypotheses: Normalized induction and unnormalized intermediate Jacquet modules are explicitly distinguished; r≥1.
proofSteps: Use the geometric descent formula on a block diagonal β and the norm integral for the étale block.
Apply twisted character–Jacquet compatibility and twisted Weyl integration to the unnormalized Jacquet-module constituents.

nodes.title: Type isolation and the trace-to-parameter reduction
nodes.statement: Let ρ be a unitary supercuspidal representation of GL_d(F), t≥2 and n=dt. Its generalized Speh Langlands quotient S is formed from ρ[(t+1)/2−i], 1≤i≤t. There is h∈C_c^∞(GL_n(O)) with tr(h|S)≠0 and tr(h|θ)=0 for every tempered irreducible θ outside the properly induced family formed from t unitary unramified twists of ρ. In particular h has zero trace on every square-integrable representation. Separately, a test function whose traces vanish on all tempered nonsquare-integrables and all generalized Speh representations has zero trace on every irreducible smooth representation. With the lower-rank character construction, Scholze Lemma 3.2 therefore reduces rank n to proper-induction traces, positive rational Weil traces for essentially square-integrable and Speh representations, and integral virtual Weil multiplicities for supercuspidals. Positivity and integrality then give actual dimension-n semisimple Weil representations.
hypotheses: Characteristic-zero admissible representations; the compact type is finite-dimensional; the density statement applies to all finite-length test traces.
proofSteps: Request the Schneider–Zink type that occurs in S and in exactly the indicated properly induced tempered family, and Kazhdan density. The compact test separates S from square-integrables; it does not isolate an essentially square-integrable unramified family.

For the vanishing criterion, take normalized constant terms along proper parabolics and apply Kazhdan density on their Levi factors. The alternating segment/Speh relation then treats square-integrables, followed by density on GL_n.

For Lemma 3.2, import the current SR.3 Bernstein centre and universal-unramified-twist APIs. The trace scalar varies regularly on each cuspidal component and descends through self twists and Weyl identifications, yielding a central multiplier. Proper induction and the compact Speh test compare its trace with f_{τ,h}; the vanishing criterion extends the identity to every constituent.
Use independence of semisimple Weil characters. Positive rational coefficients become nonnegative integers only after the independent supercuspidal integrality input.
acceptance: The compact separator has nonzero trace on S and zero trace on all square-integrables. A positive rational multiplicity 1/2 still fails the actual-representation conclusion until integrality is imposed.

The nearby cycles factor as RΨ_β⊗C_c^∞(O_{D′}×). Consequently φ_{τ,h,h′} is associated to f_{τ,h}∨×h′ in the GL_n×D′× factors. The central G_m/similitude factor is kept separately with its reciprocity character and p^{−r′}-coset; it cannot be absorbed into the GL_n parameter.

proofSteps: Use the requested structured p-divisible-group carrier and identify δ_0 up to σ-conjugacy with ((β^{-1})^t,1,β′).
Compare the ordered level bases to strict O-module levels and the étale generator set.
Tensor nearby cycles, use the étale norm identity, and apply inverse transpose to the first factor. Track the central character through Deformations Proposition 4.10 and Remark 4.11.

nodes.title: The simple unitary point count on raw cohomology
nodes.statement: On the shared early raw compact-unitary cohomology H_ξ, specialize Scholze’s auxiliary CM division data: F=F_0K, [F_0:Q] even, unitary signature (1,n−1) at one infinite place and compact at the others, D division only at the chosen conjugate split pair x,x^c, and p split in K with the selected local factor w≠x,x^c. The alternating trace tr(τ×h∨h′e_{Z_p×}f^p|H_ξ) is the weighted sum of effective Kottwitz triples with coefficient trace tr ξ(γ_0) and twisted orbital integral of φ_{τ,h,h′}. Replacing that local function by its matched transfer gives n·tr(τ×h∨h′e_{Z_p×}f^p|H_ξ)=tr(f_{τ,h}∨h′e_{p^{−r′}Z_p×}f^p|H_ξ), r′=r[κ_F:F_p]. The PEL generic fibre is a disjoint union indexed by ker^1(Q,G), not a canonically single Shimura variety.

nodes.title: Positive Weil traces from early unitary globalization
nodes.statement: For an essentially square-integrable π of GL_n(F), or a generalized Speh representation in Scholze Lemma 3.2(ii), globalize π∨ so that π_w=π∨⊗χ with χ unramified. Write W for the alternating cohomological multiplicity and a=dim(W)/n, a nonzero signed integer. Corollary 10.1 gives tr(f∨_{τ,h}|π_w)=a⁻¹tr(τ|W⊗χ_sim)tr(h∨|π_w). Using tr(f∨|π_w)=tr(f|π_w∨), the correct positive rational class is rec_un(π)=a⁻¹W⊗χ_sim⊗χ, where local characters are interpreted through geometric reciprocity. Since W occurs in a single parity, sign(a)W is effective of dimension |a|n. This yields a positive rational Weil class of dimension n. The dualized formula in the proof of Corollary 10.3 of the 2010 author copy is replaced by this direct trace calculation, as recorded in E-ET6-3.

nodes.title: Weil–Deligne local Langlands
nodes.statement: For each n≥1, LLC_WD is a bijection between irreducible smooth complex representations of GL_n(F) and n-dimensional Frobenius-semisimple WD isomorphism classes with finite inertia. It commutes with duals, character twists and field isomorphisms; det(r)=ω_π through geometric reciprocity. Standard L/epsilon and all pair L/epsilon/gamma factors agree, with full monodromy. For every generic π and ψ of conductor O, its newvector exponent equals the Artin–Deligne conductor of LLC_WD(π). Equality with a later geometric semisimple GL_n parameter is an output theorem in ES7, consuming this endpoint, not an input to its construction.
hypotheses: Same normalization, complex square root, ψ and measures throughout; the nongeneric analytic extension is the previous supplier contract.
proofSteps: The inverse multisets prove bijectivity. The supercuspidal dual/twist/determinant theorem and the standard-data dual operation extend these properties to every block and quotient.
Use analytic Langlands-quotient products and special-block products for all factor identities.
Use the generic newvector theorem and the imported WD epsilon/conductor dictionary. No argument replaces N by zero when the Weil representation is already semisimple.
acceptance: In rank one this is reciprocity with N=0. For St_2 versus trivial GL_2 the monodromy and conductor checks distinguish parameters despite identical semisimple Weil traces.

nodes.title: Jacquet–Langlands for essentially square-integrable representations
nodes.statement: For D/F a central division algebra of index d and n=rd, classical JL is a bijection from essentially square-integrable irreducible GL_r(D) representations to essentially square-integrable GL_n(F) representations, characterized by Θ_{JL(π′)}(g)=(−1)^{n−r}Θ_{π′}(g′) on corresponding regular semisimple classes whose characteristic polynomials agree. In particular it has this identity on matched elliptic classes. It commutes with central-character twists. For r=1,d=n this is the division-algebra correspondence used by the local tower argument; existence is independent of the LLC constructed here.
hypotheses: Characters are the locally integrable Harish-Chandra functions; the normalization fixes maximal compact volumes. The independently proved all-r,D classical theorem is a recorded source-access gap.
proofSteps: Import untwisted character integrability/local constancy and elliptic character orthogonality from the proposed character prefix.
Use the classical Deligne–Kazhdan–Vignéras theorem, as restated with this sign and matching in Badulescu §3.1. Its proof is not replaced by Scholze’s rank-one-division tower comparison.
Use character independence for uniqueness and the classical theorem for existence and surjectivity.
acceptance: For a quaternion division algebra and n=2,r=1, the transfer of its trivial representation is unitary St_2 and the character sign is −1.

nodes.title: The additive Langlands–Jacquet quotient
nodes.statement: For n=rd let R(GL_n(F)) and R(GL_r(D)) be finite-length Grothendieck groups. Classical JL extends to an injective additive map JL_add from the inner group to the split group by mapping each Langlands standard-module basis element to the normalized induction of its transferred essentially square-integrable blocks. Let S_{n,D} be the span of standard modules whose block ranks are not all divisible by d; these have no matching inner Levi. Then R(GL_n)=im(JL_add)⊕S_{n,D}, and the canonical surjection LJ_D is the inverse on the first summand and zero on the second. It satisfies Θ_π(g)=(−1)^{n−r}Θ_{LJ_D([π])}(g′) on matching regular semisimple classes. This LJ_D already has the classical positive normalization on essentially square-integrables; multiplying it by a second sign is wrong. Its value on an irreducible can be zero or a signed virtual combination.
hypotheses: Standard-module bases require both split and inner-form Langlands classifications; a Grothendieck class is not an irreducible representation.
proofSteps: Use the standard-module basis theorem and classical JL on its essentially square-integrable blocks to define JL_add.
Character compatibility of normalized induction gives its identity on matching classes and proves injectivity. Split the standard basis by divisibility of every block rank.
Project along S_{n,D} and invert the transferred standard basis; character independence on inner forms proves the characterization.
acceptance: No assertion that JL_add sends every irreducible to an irreducible, or that LJ_D([π]) is an actual positive representation.

nodes.title: Induction and Jacquet compatibility of the quotient
nodes.statement: In the graded finite-length representation ring R(F)=⊕_{n≥0}R(GL_n(F)), the subgroup S(D)=⊕S_{n,D}, including all degrees not divisible by d, is the Hopf ideal generated by essentially square-integrable generators of rank not divisible by d. Its quotient is the GL_r(D) graded representation ring through LJ_D. The product is normalized parabolic induction and the coproduct is the sum of semisimplified normalized Jacquet modules. For corresponding Levi partitions whose blocks all have ranks divisible by d, LJ commutes with induction and, after quotienting every tensor factor by the nonmatching ideal, with Jacquet restriction. It is not an equality of unquotiented Jacquet modules for arbitrary split partitions.
hypotheses: The degree-zero unit is retained; virtual classes, normalized induction and normalized Jacquet restriction are used throughout.
proofSteps: Use the polynomial-ring presentation by essentially square-integrable standard generators; divisibility describes the ideal and quotient product.
Compare Jacquet modules of a transferred essentially square-integrable generator, using Badulescu Lemma 3.7. Its classical DKV Lemma B.2(b) input is an explicit unread-source gap.
Extend on the standard basis through the geometric lemma; discard tensor summands with a nondivisible degree before comparing coproducts.

nodes.title: The inner-form parameter from standard data
nodes.statement: For irreducible π′ of GL_r(D), take its unique ordered inner Langlands standard data δ′_1,…,δ′_t, transfer each essentially square-integrable block by classical JL, and set LLC_D(π′)=⊕_i LLC_WD(JL(δ′_i)). This is a dimension-rd Frobenius-semisimple WD class. Its image consists exactly of WD classes each of whose indecomposable special-block dimensions is divisible by d, and its inverse uses the classical inverse on each essentially square-integrable block and the inner Langlands quotient. The split quotient Q(π′) of the transferred standard data has this same WD parameter. No general identity LJ_D([Q(π′)])=[π′] or equality JL_add([π′])=[Q(π′)] is asserted: Badulescu’s version explicitly treats the general Q character identity as a conjecture.
hypotheses: Import the all-inner-form Langlands standard-data classification as an SR.3 extension; it is stronger than a conditional general-group tempered-support contract.

nodes.title: Principal-series nontransfer and virtual cancellation
nodes.statement: For a nontrivial inner form d>1 and n divisible by d, every irreducible generic principal series induced from n rank-one characters has a full parameter with n one-dimensional, zero-monodromy blocks and hence no corresponding GL_{n/d}(D) representation under LLC_D. Its irreducible induced standard class has LJ_D=0. At a reducibility point only the entire induced standard class is killed; individual irreducible constituents can have nonzero signed transfers. For quaternion D, the reducible GL_2 standard module with constituents St_2 and 1 has LJ images +1_{D×} and −1_{D×}. The trivial GL_2 constituent has no inner parameter although its LJ image is nonzero.
hypotheses: For the first claim the normalized principal series is irreducible; at reducibility use Grothendieck additivity, not an assertion about each constituent.
proofSteps: Use the split Langlands data and WD block image criterion.
Every rank-one standard block fails divisibility by d, so the standard class belongs to ker LJ_D.
At the GL_2 reducibility point the classical St_2 transfer and the exact constituent relation determine the negative trivial-representation image.
acceptance: An assertion that every nonrelevant irreducible has zero LJ fails on trivial GL_2.

sources.match: The nonmatching standard-module kernel explains both irreducible principal-series vanishing and constituent cancellation.

nodes.title: Worked classical normalization checks
nodes.statement: Compute the following shared regression cases. An unramified GL_1 character χ(ϖ)=α has N=0, L=(1−αq^{−s})^{-1}, and conductor 0. For GL_2, the trivial representation has σ_ss=ω^{−1/2}⊕ω^{1/2}, N=0 and L=(1−q^{−s+1/2})^{-1}(1−q^{−s−1/2})^{-1}; unitary St_2 has the same σ_ss, N of rank 1, L=(1−q^{−s−1/2})^{-1} and conductor 1. For unramified θ on the Weil side of an irreducible unramified-quadratic induction, a genuinely non-Frobenius-invariant character must be ramified: an unramified character of W_E is invariant and its induction is reducible. For a regular tame character of the residue units of E, its irreducible quadratic Weil induction has N=0, no inertia invariants, L=1 and Artin conductor 2; the bijection gives its supercuspidal endpoint. Finally, at residue degree two the connected-height-one harmonic descent coefficient in rank two and r=1 is q=p², not p.
hypotheses: E/F is the unramified quadratic extension and the tame residue character satisfies θ^q≠θ; its local character extension to W_E is fixed through geometric reciprocity.
proofSteps: Evaluate the imported rank-one Euler factor and arithmetic special block at geometric Frobenius.
Use the two Langlands data multisets and ker N to compute GL_2 Euler polynomials and the monodromy conductor term.
Use induced Weil restriction on inertia, tame Swan conductor 0 and the degree-two residue cardinality to check the other two boundary calculations; the type classification is imported from SR.4.
acceptance: The tame example requires a noninvariant residue character; unramified quadratic induction of an unramified character is not a supercuspidal example.
